personality_one_liner: A cinematic, premium, and visually arresting booking experience that treats tattoo artistry with high-end editorial reverence.

spacing.rule: Generous spacing. Allow the dark negative space to highlight the photography. Sticky CTAs must have safe-area padding at the bottom.

do's: Use expo-blur for the bottom tab bar, sticky headers over scrolling content, and sticky bottom CTA containers in the booking flow.
Apply frosted glass overlays on featured artist cards sitting on photo backdrops.
Always pair text on glass with a tint base underneath for readability (>=75% opacity on dark mode).
dont's: Never blur body text regions, form fields, or standard list rows.

screens.name: Home / Discover
screens.purpose: A toggleable Map/List view for users to discover parlours and featured artists.

states.loading: Dark skeleton loaders mimicking image cards.
states.empty: Illustration of a tattoo machine with 'No parlours found in this area'.
states.error: Message 'Failed to load locations' with a retry button.

screens.layout: Sticky header with Search and 'Map/List' segmented control. Beneath, a horizontal scroll for style tags (Traditional, Realism, etc.). The list view uses edge-to-edge cards with large imagery and glassmorphism headers.

screens.name: Parlour Detail
screens.purpose: Showcase a specific tattoo parlour's vibe, artists, and reviews.

states.empty: N/A - detail data is either loaded or not.

screens.layout: Large cinematic hero image at the top with a heavy 3-stop vertical gradient scrim to black at the bottom. Floating back button. Content divided into sticky tabs (Gallery, Artists, Reviews). Sticky 'Book Now' CTA inside a glass container pinned to the bottom.

screens.name: Artist Profile
screens.purpose: A media-rich showcase of an artist's portfolio and available services.
screens.layout: Profile header (avatar in a tinted circle if no real photo, but prefer photo). A dense, masonry-style image grid for the portfolio to maximize visual impact. Sticky 'Book Artist' CTA.

screens.name: Booking Flow
screens.purpose: Step-by-step wizard to secure an appointment.

states.error: Validation errors below inputs in error color.

screens.layout: Progress indicator at the top. Single question per screen (1: Select Service, 2: Select Date/Time using a calendar grid, 3: Add Details). Sticky 'Next/Confirm' button at the bottom.

screens.name: Artist Dashboard
screens.purpose: Management hub for artists to view their schedule and requests.

states.empty: Message: 'Your schedule is clear today' with a subtle illustration.

screens.layout: Utility-first dark layout. Oversized typography for today's appointment count. List of upcoming bookings with status badges (Pending, Confirmed). Segmented controls to switch days.

instructions_to_main_agent: Adopt the '6 Glass / Luxe' dark-theme personality. The app should feel cinematic, expensive, and edgy. NEVER use blue, purple, or indigo; stick strictly to the muted champagne gold (#D9B76A) and dark charcoal/blacks.
For the typography, use Fraunces for large display headings (parlour names, titles) and Satoshi for all body text and UI labels. Ensure font weights never exceed 500.
Implement a Map + List toggle on the home screen. When showing the List, use edge-to-edge cards with high-quality images and a subtle glassmorphism overlay for the card text.

Whenever text sits on top of an image (like hero banners on the Parlour Detail screen), you MUST implement the gradient-to-dark scrim pattern (Layer 0: Image, Layer 1: expo-linear-gradient transparent to ≥70% surfaceInverse, Layer 2: Text).

The Booking Flow must be broken down into single-question steps to reduce cognitive load. Ensure the 'Next' or 'Confirm' CTA is sticky at the bottom, wrapped in a frosted glass container over any scrolling content.
On the Artist Dashboard, lean slightly into utility with oversized metrics, but keep the luxe aesthetic with sharp borders and clean typography.
Ensure all primary interactive components (tabs, main CTAs) have haptic feedback wired up.
Do not use generic system alerts for errors; build cohesive full-screen Error/Empty states using the dark palette and muted gold accents.
